tier_reason: C stands; the random-decode column is invalid (it mostly times clock reads) and the baseline is corrected to the shipped LUT Shifted default.

corrections.baseline: libmorton's shipped non-BMI default (LUT Shifted) and its other LUT methods, as measured in morton-nd's fork of the libmorton test harness
corrections.caveats: Enricher: the kevinhartman/libmorton harness wraps every 8-code block, and every single code in random decode, in two clock_gettime calls through function pointers, so the random-decode rows (3.1-4.5 s for all methods) time clock reads and their 1.14x is meaningless; against LUT Shifted BMI2 gives 1.19x/1.58x encode and 1.55x/2.32x decode (32/64-bit, linear). The AVX512 path is unreachable when BMI2 is available; pdep/pext are slow on Zen 1 and 2; glibc uint_fast32_t is 8 bytes, so 32-bit calls run 64-bit loops on Linux.
